podcast.title: Biggest Black Vocal Group
podcast.body: The Dominoes were recognized as the biggest black vocal group of the early 1950s. "They were the biggest black vocal group of the early 50s."

podcast.title: Chart Decline Post-McPhatter
podcast.body: After Clyde McPhatter's departure, The Dominoes began to experience less success in the charts, having no hits at all in 1954. "Their records weren't telling as well as they had been when Clyde McFatter was the group lead singer, and in 1954 they had no hits at all."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Discipline from Ward
podcast.body: Billy Ward taught Jackie Wilson breath control and provided him with much-needed discipline, becoming a father figure. "Ward taught in breath control and became something of a father figure, giving him some discipline for the first time in his life."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Focus on Live Performances
podcast.body: The group's strategy was not solely to succeed as recording artists but also as live performers, securing a lucrative two-year residency in Las Vegas. "The group weren't just looking to have success as recording artists, but as live performers."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-Four: "Reet Petite" by Jackie Wilson

podcast.title: Huge Influence on Soul Music
podcast.body: Billy Ward and The Dominoes were a massive influence on the development of soul music. Their lead singers, Clyde McFatter and Jackie Wilson, sang in a style heavily indebted to the church music that the Isley Brothers had also performed, making them a natural inspiration for the Isley Brothers' transition from gospel to doo-wop. "Billy Ward and the Dominoes were a huge influence on the music that became soal, with hit records like Have Mercy Baby."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Jackie Wilson's Departure
podcast.body: Jackie Wilson decided to leave the group in 1957 because it became apparent that Billy Ward's ambitions extended no further than continuing to play Las Vegas indefinitely, earning vast amounts of money without hard work or travel, while Wilson desired more from his career. "It had become a pament that Ward had no bigger ambitions than to keep playing Las Vegas forever, and keep making vast amounts of money without having to travel or work especially hard."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Leader Billy Ward as Vocal Coach
podcast.body: The group was led by Billy Ward, who served as a vocal coach and was not their lead singer. "They were led by Billy Ward, a vocal coach who was not their lead singer."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Lucrative Las Vegas Residency
podcast.body: The Dominoes secured a two-year residency in Las Vegas, supporting Louis Prima and Keely Smith, earning a massive $5,000 a week, though most of this went to Ward. "They got a two year residency in Las Vegas, supporting Louis Prima in Keely Smith. The group were getting $5,000 a week, at massive amount of money in those days."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-Four: "Reet Petite" by Jackie Wilson

podcast.title: Replacing Clyde McPhatter
podcast.body: Jackie Wilson was brought into the group as a replacement for Clyde McPhatter, who was getting restless, with Wilson studying McPhatter's style for weeks before taking his place. "He decided to get Wilson into the group as a replacement for McFatter, though McFatter and Wilson were in the group together for a while, as McFatter served out his notice with the group."
